from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vectors are arrows in a 2D plane.", "Point (x, y) uses basis vectors i-hat and j-hat.", "Any vector is a linear combination of basis vectors."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: Vectors as Coordinates", lecture_lines)

        # Prepare objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.7)
        i_hat = Vector([1, 0], color="#FF0000")
        j_hat = Vector([0, 1], color="#00FF00")
        i_label = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color="#FF0000").next_to(i_hat.get_end(), RIGHT)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color="#00FF00").next_to(j_hat.get_end(), UP)
        v = Vector([2, 3], color="#FFFFFF")
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}").to_edge(DOWN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(axes, i_hat, j_hat, i_label, j_label), 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(i_hat), Write(i_label), FadeIn(j_hat), Write(j_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000") # Use red for i_hat reference

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(v), Write(v_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00") # Use green for combination reference
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Linear transformations move vectors within space.",
            "The origin point must remain fixed.",
            "Grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining Linear Transformation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create grid
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.5}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(plane, "A1", "F6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform the grid
        matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        new_plane = plane.copy().apply_matrix(matrix)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Transform(plane, new_plane))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        label = Text("Linear Transformation", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A3")
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Matrices track where basis vectors i-hat and j-hat land.",
            "Columns define the destination of basis vectors.",
            "All points transform based on these new basis positions.",
            "Visual demonstration of basis movement.",
            "Linear combinations map the entire space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Matrix as a Transformation Recipe", lecture_lines)
        
        # --- Prepare Visuals ---
        # Matrix M = [[2, 0], [0, 1]]
        matrix = MathTex(r"M = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Basis vectors
        i_vec = Vector(RIGHT, color=RED)
        j_vec = Vector(UP, color=GREEN)
        
        basis_group = VGroup(i_vec, j_vec)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_group, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(basis_group))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # i moves to (2,0)
        i_target = Vector([2, 0], color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(i_target, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Transform(i_vec, i_target))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # j stays at (0,1)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Composition", [
            "Matrix multiplication applies two transformations sequentially.",
            "Order of operations significantly changes the final result.",
            "Rotation then shear differs from shear then rotation."
        ])
        
        # Define visual elements
        square_a = Square(side_length=1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        square_b = Square(side_length=1, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(square_a, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(square_b, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.add(square_a, square_b)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Animate sequence
        self.play(
            square_a.animate.rotate(PI/4),
            square_b.animate.apply_matrix([[1, 0.5], [0, 1]]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Highlight transformation
        self.play(
            square_a.animate.set_stroke(color=RED, width=4),
            square_b.animate.set_stroke(color=RED, width=4),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Linear Transformations and Matrices: The Geometry of Change

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Coordinates
sections.content: Briefly define a vector as an arrow in a 2D plane (x, y). Establish that any point can be described by a linear combination of basis vectors î (1,0) and ĵ (0,1). This visual foundation is critical for understanding what happens when space is 'warped'.
sections.example: Visualizing a character position as a vector starting at the origin (0,0) and ending at (2,3).

sections.title: Defining Linear Transformation
sections.content: Explain that a linear transformation is a function that takes an input vector and outputs a new vector. Two golden rules: 1) The origin remains fixed. 2) Grid lines remain parallel and evenly spaced. Use an animation of a 'stretching' or 'rotating' grid to demonstrate these rules.
sections.example: An animation of a robot's arm movement where the base remains fixed while the tip follows a straight-line path.

sections.title: The Matrix as a Transformation Recipe
sections.content: Reveal the core concept: a matrix is simply a container for the 'destinations' of basis vectors î and ĵ. By showing where î and ĵ land after a transformation, we can determine where every other point in space lands using matrix-vector multiplication.
sections.example: The matrix [[2, 0], [0, 1]] shows î moves to (2,0) and ĵ stays at (0,1), visually stretching a square into a rectangle.

sections.title: Visualizing Composition
sections.content: Explain matrix multiplication as applying two transformations in sequence. Crucially, emphasize that order matters: applying a rotation then a shear is visually distinct from a shear then a rotation.
sections.example: A cat character flipping (rotation matrix) and then widening (scaling matrix) vs. widening then flipping.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Conclude by highlighting that matrices are the engine behind computer graphics. Games use these transformations to move characters and render 3D worlds in real-time.
sections.example: A brief montage of a 3D gaming model moving through a scene, with the corresponding matrix changing values dynamically.
